item.title: Kema Sakuranomiya Park: Osaka's Great Riverside Cherry Avenue — Guide
item.description: Kema Sakuranomiya Park stretches for several kilometres along both banks of the Okawa river north of central Osaka, and in early April it becomes one of the city’s most spectacular places to see cherry blossom. Nearly five thousand trees form near-continuous tunnels of pink along the water, best appreciated on a slow walk from Sakuranomiya Station toward the old Mint Bureau, whose private cherry avenue opens to the public for a famous week each spring.

item.title: Ozu Castle and Cormorant Fishing — Guide
item.description: Ozu Castle stands above the Hiji River in the castle town of Ozu, sometimes called ‘little Kyoto’ for its old streets and riverside setting. Unusually, its four-storey wooden keep was faithfully reconstructed in the early 2000s using traditional methods and authentic materials, making it one of Japan’s most convincing modern wooden castle rebuilds — you can even stay overnight in the keep as a special experience. In summer, the river below comes alive with ukai, traditional cormorant fishing, in which fishermen in boats use trained cormorants to catch sweetfish by torchlight, a spectacle watched from pleasure boats.

item.title: Kitakami Tenshochi: Iwate's Riverside Cherry Tunnel — Guide
item.description: Stretching two kilometres along the Kitakami River, Tenshochi Park is lined with 10,000 Yoshino cherry trees that form a blossoming tunnel each April. Rent a rowboat to drift beneath the overhanging branches, or ride the little steam train through the park. Blossoms reflected in the river with the distant Kitakami mountains make this one of Tohoku’s most beloved spring walks. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kitakami, Iwate Hours Park always open; festival late Apr Admission Free (boat/train extra) Time needed 1.

item.title: Nakanoshima Guide: Osaka's Riverside Island of Art & Architecture
item.description: A long, slender island between two rivers in the heart of Osaka, Nakanoshima is the city’s most refined district — a calm, green ribbon of historic architecture, art museums, and riverside promenades that feels worlds away from the noise of Minami. Here the stately red-brick Osaka City Central Public Hall anchors a cluster of galleries, a famous rose garden, leafy walkways, and stylish waterside cafes. It’s where Osaka comes to slow down, stroll, and look at art and the water.
